title: Internal Chargeback & Customer Billing Guidelines (2026)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the standardized approach for internal product chargebacks, customer billing edge-case handling, revenue recognition interactions, and forecast reconciliation. It consolidates the cross-functional steps required between Finance, Legal, Sales Ops, and Engineering for consistent invoicing, deferred revenue accounting, and dispute resolution.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference hosted invoicing, internal product cost chargebacks to business units (BU), and contract amendments that affect billing or rev rec. Excludes payroll and non-operational corporate allocations.

Key principles

- Accuracy first: invoices and internal chargebacks must map directly to contract terms or signed amendments.
- Deterministic calculation: rates, rounding rules, and proration logic must be codified and automated where possible.
- Clear ownership: each stage has a single accountable owner (see "Roles and ownership").
- Auditability: maintain an immutable record (invoice json + reconciled ledger entries + decision log) for each billing period.

Roles and ownership

- Finance (Billing & RevRec): Owner of invoice templates, GL mapping, revenue recognition rules, monthly close. Responsible for final invoice approval and journal entries.
- Sales Ops: Contract intake, CLM updates, and dispute facilitation. Responsible for ensuring signed SOWs/AMEND addenda are attached to account records.
- Legal: Contract language review for non-standard billing terms (termination credits, milestone invoicing, rebates).
- Engineering (Billing Platform Team): Responsible for implementation of pricing/usage meters, rate-limiter configs, and export of usage reports to billing pipeline.
- Customer Success / Account Owner: First-line contact for customer disputes.

Internal chargeback model (for BU cost allocation)

Purpose: Distribute hosted/shared platform and infrastructure costs back to product teams and internal consumers to drive visibility into unit economics.

Chargeback cadence: Monthly, with a 10-business-day lag to allow for usage collection and validation.

Chargeback rate components: 
- Compute pool (per-GPU-hour equivalent)
- Storage (per-GB-month)
- Networking (per-GB egress)
- Platform flat fee (per-tenant-month)

Example chargeback rate table (effective 2026-01):

| Cost component        | Unit             | Rate (USD) |
|-----------------------|------------------|------------|
| Compute (reserved)    | GPU-hour equiv.  | 2.30       |
| Compute (burst)       | GPU-hour equiv.  | 3.75       |
| Storage               | GB-month         | 0.012      |
| Networking (egress)   | GB               | 0.045      |
| Platform fee          | tenant-month     | 150.00     |

Chargeback calculation rules:

1) Usage is sourced from the billing export CSV (engineering-billing/export/YYYY-MM).
2) Apply SKU-level rate mapping; if SKU is unmapped, default to platform fee bucket and create a billing ticket.
3) Round computed USD to 2 decimal places; bucket at the resource line item level.
4) When a resource spans multiple BUs, apply allocation tags (team:tag) with percent splits recorded in the usage export. If tags are missing, the default allocation is 100% to the owning tenant.
5) Disputes to chargebacks must be raised within 7 business days of chargeback distribution; after 30 days, adjustments require a formal journal correction.

Customer billing & invoice lifecycle

Invoice generation flow (high-level):

1. Usage collection: Engineering exports usage snapshots at the system boundary (UTC-based daily usage).
2. Pre-bill validation: Billing team runs validation scripts (schema checks, volume anomalies, negative usage anomalies).
3. Draft invoice creation: Automated generator creates a draft invoice (JSON) with line items, taxes, and payment terms.
4. Review & approval: Finance reviews high-dollar (>USD 50k) or anomalous invoices.
5. Dispatch: Send PDF and structured invoice JSON to customer billing email and SFTP endpoint (if configured).
6. Receipt & reconciliation: Payments posted by AR and matched to invoices.

Invoice contents requirements:

- Invoice ID (RFC4122 UUID format)
- Customer account ID and billing contact
- Billing period start/end (ISO8601)
- Line items with SKU, quantity, unit_price, amount, and source reference (usage-report-id)
- Payment terms (Net 30 / Net 45 / prepay)
- Tax breakdown where applicable (country- and VAT-level codes)
- Reference to signed contract id and amendment id (if any)

Sample invoice JSON snippet (for developer reference, 1-line string in actual system):
{
  "invoice_id": "7f8b2c2e-3a5d-4bfa-9f77-a2e9bf3e9021",
  "account_id": "acct_82XY7",
  "period_start": "2026-02-01",
  "period_end": "2026-02-28",
  "line_items": [ ... ]
}

Revenue recognition interplay

General rules:
- Usage-based revenue (hosted API tokens, embeddings units) is recognized as earned in the period when the usage occurs.
- Prepaid credits (customer prepays) are deferred to a contract liability and recognized as usage occurs (system posts deferred revenue) per ASC 606 principles.
- Milestone and committed capacity contracts are recognized pro rata over the service period unless contract terms specify milestone-based recognition approved by RevRec.

Journal entry examples:

1) Customer prepays $100k on 2026-02-15 (initial entry):
- Dr Cash 100,000
- Cr Deferred Revenue 100,000

2) During Feb 2026, usage consumes $18,450 of credits (recognize revenue):
- Dr Deferred Revenue 18,450
- Cr Revenue - Hosted API 18,450

3) Monthly invoice for usage billed Net 30 on 2026-02-28 for $22,000 (AR posting):
- Dr Accounts Receivable 22,000
- Cr Revenue - Hosted API 22,000

Contract amendment & credits workflow

When a contract amendment affects billing (rate change, refund, or credit):

1. Sales Ops attaches signed amendment to CLM and tags account with amendment_id.
2. Sales Ops notifies Billing team via #billing-ops Slack channel and opens a Billing Adjustment ticket (JIRA/BILL-xxx). Include effective_date and accounting treatment requested.
3. Finance evaluates impact on deferred revenue and determines whether a correction or waiver is appropriate.
4. If a credit is customer-facing, issue credit memo referencing original invoice and record the corresponding AR/Revenue reversal entries.

Credit memo accounting example (USD 1,200 credit applied to invoice INV-2026-0023):
- Dr Revenue - Hosted API 1,200
- Cr Accounts Receivable 1,200

Billing dispute SLA and escalation

- First response: within 2 business days (Account Owner).
- Investigation resolution target: 10 business days for standard disputes; 30 business days for complex contract-level disputes requiring legal review.
- Interim adjustments: temporary credit can be issued at Finance’s discretion to prevent operational impact, documented with a follow-up postmortem and reversal if dispute is resolved against the customer.

Escalation path:

1) Customer -> Account Owner
2) Account Owner -> Billing Operations (Finance)
3) Billing Operations -> Sales Ops + Legal (if contractual)
4) Finance VP -> CFO (if >USD 250k or material to monthly close)

Forecasting and reconciliation process (monthly close)

1) Day 1-3: Finalize usage extraction and run anomaly detection.
2) Day 4-7: Draft revenue recognition run for the period; flag any open prepays or credits.
3) Day 8-10: Reconcile AR ledger to bank and payment processors.
4) Day 11-14: Close revenue and post journal entries.

Forecast reconciliation checklist:

- Compare billed usage vs. usage-based revenue recognized (delta explained by timing or credits).
- Reconcile deferred revenue balances to contract liabilities register.
- Summarize large variances (>5% month-over-month or >USD 50k) with root cause and owner.
- Sign-offs: Billing Manager + Head of RevRec.

Automation and tooling standards

Required exports and formats:
- Usage export: CSV with headers [date, account_id, sku, quantity, allocation_tags, report_id].
- Invoice artifact: PDF + structured invoice JSON (schema v2).
- Journal export: CSV ledger with [date, gl_account, debit, credit, memo, ref_invoice_id].

Monitoring & alerts:
- Billing platform should alert on: negative-usage, >3x day-over-day usage spike per account, orphan line-items (no mapped contract id), and failed invoice generation.
- Finance must subscribe to PagerDuty for system outages that block invoice dispatch.

Security and data residency

- All invoice artifacts are classified as PII-sensitive where they contain billing contact details and must be stored in the restricted S3 bucket (finance-invoices-restricted) with KMS encryption.
- Export of invoice JSON to customer SFTP endpoints must be over TLS and limited to customer-approved destinations configured in CLM.

Change control and review cycle

- Pricing or chargeback rate changes require: Finance proposal -> Modeling run (impact on margin & revenue) -> Legal review (contract language impact) -> 30-day notice to affected customers (if contractually required) -> Prod rollout by Engineering.
- This document review cadence: annual review in November and ad-hoc updates for major policy changes.

Appendix: Common edge cases and decisions

Q: How to treat overage for Dedicated customers who exceed committed throughput?
A: Overage is billed at the burst compute rate for the month and recognized as usage revenue. If the customer disputes measurement, initiate meter audit (Engineering) and hold the disputed balance pending audit (max 30 days).

Q: How are refunds for on-demand billing handled?
A: Refunds are rare; prefer credit memo application to future invoices. Refunds require CFO sign-off if >USD 5k.

Q: Inter-company allocations for global regions?
A: Use the master SLA currency conversion table; chargebacks to regional entities are performed in local currency at month-end FX rates published by Treasury.
